public.title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
public.description: Given valid preorder and inorder traversals of the same binary tree with distinct integer values, return its compact breadth-first encoding with trailing nulls removed. Empty traversals produce []. Both arrays have equal length, at most 200, with values from -10000 to 10000. Trees use compact breadth-first arrays: the first value is the root; each non-null node consumes the next two entries as left and right children. Null marks a missing child; trailing nulls may be omitted. Empty arrays mean no tree. Values are integers from -10000 to 10000, with at most 200 nodes.
hints: The next preorder value is the root; its inorder position splits its children.
public.attribution: Original Bekor statement, examples, tests and solutions, 2026. Adapted from a standard algorithmic problem; no third-party exercise text used.

explanation: Recursively split inorder ranges using a value-to-position map and consume preorder roots. Serialize with breadth-first traversal. O(n) time and space.
